newEvents.event: An independent inspection vendor and the homeowner confirmed a property inspection for September 22.
The property inspection took place with the vendor and the homeowner.
The inspection vendor sent the photos from the September 22 inspection.
Joseph sent his position to the carrier's adjuster: the estimate and the photo report, and requested a re-inspection.
The carrier's adjuster declined to change the estimate and offered to meet for a re-inspection.
The re-inspection did not happen because Joseph did not attend the appointment the carrier's adjuster had confirmed.
Since the carrier would not grant a re-inspection, Joseph submitted a formal appraisal demand on the insured's behalf.
The carrier rejected the appraisal demand, saying it needed to be signed by all named insureds and accompanied by the repair estimate.
Joseph disputed the carrier's position and said he would have the other named insured sign the demand and send the estimate.
Joseph told the carrier to name an appraiser within 20 days or he would petition for a court-appointed umpire.
The carrier acknowledged the signed appraisal demand and asked for the estimate; Joseph sent his position: the estimate and the photo report.
The carrier's adjuster asked to schedule a re-inspection before management would approve appraisal, and Joseph scheduled it for February 20.
Joseph formally requested that the carrier pay statutory prompt-payment interest under the Texas Insurance Code for the delay in paying the claim.
The carrier responded that no interest was due because no appraisal award was issued and payment had been made promptly.
Joseph acknowledged the carrier's position.
The carrier issued payment on the claim.
The carrier requested a completed W-9 form for tax reporting on the payment issued.

results.update: The claim reached appraisal after the carrier repeatedly declined re-inspection; the carrier issued payment on the claim in June and is now asking Joseph to submit a completed W-9 for its tax reporting. Nothing further is needed from the referring party.
